tier_reason: Independent third-party run (nigeltao/qoir, not the QOI author) with public benchmark code (test/benchmarks.c, adapter/qoi_adapter.c, adapter/png_libpng_adapter.c, script/run_full_benchmarks.sh), compiler gcc 10.2.1, flags -Wall -O3 plus -march=native for the adapters, and CPU i5-10210U stated; the QOI row (146.87 / 193.53 MPixels/s) and PNG/libpng row (5.49 / 56.18) of the top-level images/ block match the record.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: gcc (Debian 10.2.1-6) 10.2.1; script/run_full_benchmarks.sh defaults CFLAGS to '-Wall -O3' and compiles adapter/qoi_adapter.c (which builds the vendored third_party/qoi/qoi.h) with -march=native -Wall -O3; libpng and libwebp are Debian Bullseye system packages (their build flags are not stated)
corrections.caveats: QOI is a different file format from PNG (readers need QOI support) and trades compression for speed: overall CmpRatio 0.2823 vs libpng 0.2423 (QOI output about 17% larger, derived from page data) and vs WebP lossless 0.1651; QOI compresses worse than libpng on every subset row of doc/full_benchmarks.txt (for example photo_wikipedia 0.6618 vs 0.5663, photo_kodak 0.5829 vs 0.5630). The libpng baseline (PNG/libpng row, 'Debian Bullseye's libpng' per the file's Notes) is the distro package driven through the simplified API: adapter/png_libpng_adapter.c calls png_image_write_to_memory with image.flags = 0, so PNG_IMAGE_FLAG_FAST is not set and libpng runs at its defaults (zlib default compression level, all-filters heuristic), i.e. its default compression level, not a speed-tuned setting. Timing in test/benchmarks.c: 5 repetitions per image with gettimeofday, single-threaded, allocation included; the harness does not compare decoded pixels with the source (no round-trip check). The WebP_Lossless row uses libpng for images with a dimension above 16383 px, and the WebP decode adapter adds a full-image memcpy. The vendored qoi.h differs from current upstream only by the April 2025 modulo-to-mask change (about 1.4% faster encoding) and stricter qoi_read/qoi_write file-I/O error checks, so the numbers still represent current code. The phoboslab/qoi README itself has no numbers: it says compression is 'usually worse than libPNG' while 'throughput is a lot higher' and links qoiformat.org/benchmark (egress-blocked, not opened); its first-party qoibench.c benchmarks stbi, libpng and QOI. The fpng README (richgel999/fpng) measured QOI at 83.90 and 138.18 MP/s against stb_image and lodepng, not libpng. WangXuan95/Image-Compression-Benchmark (CLIC2021, i7-12700H, Windows 10, Pillow PNG rather than libpng, times include process startup) lists QOI at 19.061 compress and 18.970 decompress time vs PNG (optimize=False) 334.791 and 33.677 (lower is better, unit not stated).

notes: Checked rows: images/ block lines 65 (PNG/libpng 0.2423, 5.49, 56.18) and 68 (QOI 0.2823, 146.87, 193.53); baseline is Debian Bullseye's libpng at its default compression settings. Metadata confirmed on github.com: MIT, 7.5k stars, not archived, not a fork, last commit 2026-09-27; the '40+ language ports' figure was not counted.

corrections.caveats: QOIR is a different, experimental file format ('subject to incompatible changes'), not PNG. Compression trade-off: overall CmpRatio 0.2525 vs libpng 0.2423 (QOIR output about 4% larger, derived from page data; the README gives libpng 0.960 relative) and vs WebP lossless 0.1651; QOIR is larger than libpng on the photo_tecnick (0.5642 vs 0.5011), photo_wikipedia (0.6145 vs 0.5663), textures_photo (0.6052 vs 0.5977) and pngimg (0.1747 vs 0.1703) subsets and smaller on photo_kodak (0.5345 vs 0.5630) and screenshot_web (0.0710 vs 0.0757). The libpng baseline (PNG/libpng row, 'Debian Bullseye's libpng' per the file's Notes) is the distro package driven through the simplified API: adapter/png_libpng_adapter.c calls png_image_write_to_memory with image.flags = 0, so PNG_IMAGE_FLAG_FAST is not set and libpng runs at its defaults (zlib default compression level, all-filters heuristic), i.e. its default compression level, not a speed-tuned setting. Timing in test/benchmarks.c: 5 repetitions per image with gettimeofday, single-threaded, allocation included; the harness does not compare decoded pixels with the source (no round-trip check). The WebP_Lossless row uses libpng for images with a dimension above 16383 px, and the WebP decode adapter adds a full-image memcpy. Author's own benchmark (December 2022 run); one laptop-class CPU (i5-10210U) and gcc 10.2.1. The only later src/qoir.h change (2026-07-07, ce7b583, 'Fix qoir_chunk_payload_len vs src_len check') relaxes an over-strict length check that rejected some valid tiny files and does not affect the measured numbers. In the same table Wuffs' PNG decoder decodes at 140.79 MPixels/s (vs libpng 56.18), and the README says ZPNG is 'very competitive with and sometimes strictly better than QOIR'. AVIF was not measured (author hit Debian bug 976349), so there is no libavif comparison. An independent suite (WangXuan95/Image-Compression-Benchmark, CLIC2021, i7-12700H, Windows 10, Pillow PNG not libpng, times include process startup) lists QOIR at 23.696 compress and 19.752 decompress time vs PNG (optimize=False) 334.791 and 33.677 (lower is better, unit not stated).

corrections.compiler_and_flags: gcc (Debian 10.2.1-6) 10.2.1; script/run_full_benchmarks.sh defaults CFLAGS to '-Wall -O3' and compiles adapter/zpng_adapter.cpp (which includes the vendored third_party/zpng/zpng.cpp) with -march=native -Wall -O3; zstd, libpng and libwebp are Debian Bullseye system packages (their build flags are not stated); Zpng calls zstd at level 1
corrections.caveats: Zpng is its own format (custom header plus zstd), not PNG-compatible. Compression trade-off: overall CmpRatio 0.2182 vs libpng 0.2423 (smaller), and smaller than libpng on every subset row checked (for example photo_kodak 0.4776 vs 0.5630, screenshot_web 0.0584 vs 0.0757), but WebP lossless is smaller still (0.1651). The libpng baseline (PNG/libpng row, 'Debian Bullseye's libpng' per the file's Notes) is the distro package driven through the simplified API: adapter/png_libpng_adapter.c calls png_image_write_to_memory with image.flags = 0, so PNG_IMAGE_FLAG_FAST is not set and libpng runs at its defaults (zlib default compression level, all-filters heuristic), i.e. its default compression level, not a speed-tuned setting. Timing in test/benchmarks.c: 5 repetitions per image with gettimeofday, single-threaded, allocation included; the harness does not compare decoded pixels with the source (no round-trip check). The WebP_Lossless row uses libpng for images with a dimension above 16383 px, and the WebP decode adapter adds a full-image memcpy. The measured code is nigeltao/qoir's vendored third_party/zpng/zpng.cpp, identical to catid/Zpng HEAD except for an added noFilter flag (and a header bit) used only by the ZPNG_NofilLsl variant; the adapter copies the output buffer once more in both encode and decode, which slightly penalizes ZPNG. Zpng depends on the zstd library. The Zpng README itself claims 'less than 6% of the time of a PNG compressor and a file that is 66% of the size' (248.737 ms vs 4339.82 ms on one JPEG-derived image), without naming the PNG library. Image-Compression-Benchmark (CLIC2021, i7-12700H, Windows 10, Pillow PNG not libpng, times include process startup) lists ZPNG at 25.909 compress and 24.083 decompress time vs PNG (optimize=False) 334.791 and 33.677 (lower is better, unit not stated).
